resources.title: llamafile model engine
resources.description: Mozilla.ai's llamafile 0.10.6: one portable program that runs language models on Windows, macOS and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64), on the processor or a supported graphics card. Arcana starts it only while answering questions, on this computer only, and stops it when idle. Needed by the local question-answering models.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.notes: llamafile is Apache-2.0; it bundles llama.cpp (MIT) and Cosmopolitan Libc (ISC).

warnings.text: Some antivirus programs flag llamafile's portable executable format (when checked on 23 November 2026, 1 of 76 VirusTotal engines did). Arcana verifies the file against Mozilla.ai's published SHA-256 before using it.

resources.title: Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct (tiny model)
resources.description: The smallest model: answers in seconds even on a Raspberry Pi 5 or an old laptop (about 1 GB of memory), but misreads passages more often. Good for trying the assistant.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.notes: Model weights released by the Qwen team under Apache-2.0.

warnings.text: Answers come from a small language model reading passages of your library. It can misread or leave things out: check the cited passages before acting, especially for medical, legal or safety questions.

resources.title: Granite 3.3 2B Instruct (balanced model)
resources.description: IBM's small model trained for answering from supplied documents with citations. Needs about 3 GB of memory; a good default for most laptops.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.notes: Model weights released by IBM under Apache-2.0.

warnings.text: Answers come from a small language model reading passages of your library. It can misread or leave things out: check the cited passages before acting, especially for medical, legal or safety questions.

resources.title: Qwen3 4B (larger model)
resources.description: Better answers and more languages, for computers with 8 GB of memory or more. Slower on the processor alone.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.notes: Model weights released by the Qwen team under Apache-2.0.

warnings.text: Answers come from a small language model reading passages of your library. It can misread or leave things out: check the cited passages before acting, especially for medical, legal or safety questions.

resources.title: Translation engine (Bergamot)
resources.description: Mozilla's Bergamot translation engine, the WebAssembly build Firefox uses for its own offline translations. It runs inside the reader's browser, so pages are translated on the device reading them, with nothing sent anywhere. Needed by the translation language packs.

license.name: Mozilla Public License 2.0

resources.title: Kolibri classroom (Khan Academy)
resources.description: Learning Equality's Kolibri 0.19.5, with Python 3.11 for Windows, macOS and Linux, so the drive works on any computer. Arcana runs it for classes: students watch, read and practise Khan Academy and other courses, and teachers make lessons and quizzes and follow each student's progress. Set it up from the Classroom page, which also chooses the Khan Academy grades and subjects to download.

license.name: MIT License
license.notes: Kolibri is MIT and bundles its dependencies under their own licences (Django BSD-3-Clause and others). Python is under the PSF License. Khan Academy courses imported into Kolibri are CC BY-NC-SA: non-commercial use only.

resources.title: FM 4-25.11 First Aid (U.S. Army)
resources.description: The Army's first aid manual for people who are not medics: evaluating a casualty, restoring breathing, controlling bleeding, preventing shock, wounds, burns, fractures, heat and cold injuries, bites and stings, and moving a casualty. With Change 1 (2004).
resources.publisher: Headquarters, Department of the Army (United States)

license.name: US federal government work (public domain in the US)
license.notes: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). The manual states: approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

warnings.text: Military first aid from 2002–2004, not current medical advice. Some practices have changed since (the Army replaced this manual with TC 4-02.1 in 2016). In an emergency, contact emergency services or a qualified clinician whenever possible.
Superseded edition, kept because it is public domain and widely used for training.

resources.title: ATP 3-50.21 Survival (U.S. Army)
resources.description: The Army's current survival manual (September 2018): survival planning and kits, medicine in the field, shelter, water, food, fire, navigation, signaling, and survival in cold, desert, tropical and maritime environments.
resources.publisher: Headquarters, Department of the Army (United States)

license.name: US federal government work (public domain in the US)
license.notes: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). The manual states: approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

warnings.text: The medical chapter is field guidance for isolated personnel, not current medical advice. Get qualified help whenever you can.
Written for military personnel; some sections concern evading capture.

resources.title: FM 3-25.26 Map Reading and Land Navigation (U.S. Army)
resources.description: Reading topographic maps, grid coordinates, scale and distance, direction and the compass, elevation and relief, terrain association, and navigating on foot and in vehicles, by day and by night (July 2001).
resources.publisher: Headquarters, Department of the Army (United States)

license.name: US federal government work (public domain in the US)
license.notes: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). The manual states: approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

warnings.text: Edition of 2001: map, compass and terrain skills are unchanged, but the sections on GPS and electronic equipment are dated.

Columbia Pictures, black and white.

resources.title: CyberChef

resources.title: IT Tools
resources.description: IT Tools 2024.10.22: about 80 small tools for developers and administrators, such as converters, generators (UUIDs, passwords, QR codes), network calculators and text utilities, in the browser.

resources.title: Excalidraw
resources.description: Excalidraw (build 4bfc5bb of November 2021, the one Project NOMAD ships): a whiteboard for hand-drawn sketches, diagrams and plans. Drawings stay in the browser that made them; save them as files to keep or share. Live collaboration needs Excalidraw's servers and does not work offline.

license.name: MIT License
license.notes: The site is one layer of Excalidraw's official image excalidraw/excalidraw:sha-4bfc5bb on Docker Hub (Excalidraw publishes no other build of the app); mirror.gcr.io, Google's Docker Hub mirror, serves the same digest when Docker Hub limits downloads.

resources.title: Meshtastic Web
resources.description: Meshtastic's web client 2.7.1: connect to a Meshtastic radio over USB or Bluetooth from the browser to send messages, see nodes and change the radio's settings. Needs Chrome or Edge, opened on the computer running Arcana or over Arcana's HTTPS address.

license.name: GNU General Public License v3.0

resources.title: MeshCore Web
resources.description: The MeshCore companion app 1.45.0 for the browser: connect to a MeshCore radio over USB or Bluetooth to send messages and manage contacts, channels and repeaters. Needs Chrome or Edge, opened on the computer running Arcana or over Arcana's HTTPS address. Arcana downloads it from its author's site.

license.name: MeshCore companion app: closed source, free to use
license.notes: The author publishes the app as closed source and free for anyone to use, with no license to redistribute it. Arcana does not ship it: each library downloads it from files.liamcottle.net. The two fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans Symbols; SIL OFL 1.1) come from Google Fonts, from which the app would otherwise load them at run time.

warnings.text: Closed source. Its author lets anyone use it but grants no right to pass it on, so Arcana downloads it from the author's site for this library. Remove it before copying this library for someone else.

resources.title: File Browser
resources.description: File Browser 2.63.23: upload, download, rename and share files in a folder on the drive (Arcana/user/files) from any browser. Arcana creates its administrator account and shows you the password.

license.name: Apache License 2.0

resources.title: Homebox
resources.description: Homebox 0.26.2: an inventory of what you own and store, with locations, labels, quantities, photos, warranties and maintenance. Its data stays on the drive.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
license.notes: AGPL-3.0: Arcana runs the publisher's unmodified program, so section 13 (offering source to network users) asks nothing more of Arcana; the source is at the publisher's repository.

resources.title: Vaultwarden
resources.description: Vaultwarden 1.36.0 with the Bitwarden web vault: a password manager that Bitwarden's apps and browser extensions can use, kept on the drive. Linux only: Vaultwarden publishes its server only as Linux container images. Its web vault works only over HTTPS, so it needs Arcana's HTTPS (Server page).

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
license.notes: Server and web vault are layers of the official image vaultwarden/server:1.36.0-alpine (ghcr.io/dani-garcia/vaultwarden), whose server is a static Linux program. The web vault (bw_web_builds) is GPL-3.0. AGPL-3.0: Arcana runs the publisher's unmodified program, so section 13 (offering source to network users) asks nothing more of Arcana; the source is at the publisher's repository.

resources.title: Jellyfin
resources.description: Jellyfin 10.11.11 with jellyfin-ffmpeg 7.1.4: a media server for your own films, series, music and photos, with apps for phones and televisions. Put media in Arcana/user/files/Media (File Browser can upload it) and add that folder as a library in Jellyfin.

license.name: GNU General Public License v2.0
license.notes: jellyfin-ffmpeg is GPL-3.0. Jellyfin's Windows build carries its own copy; the other platforms get the portable build.

resources.title: Calibre-Web
resources.description: Calibre-Web 0.6.26, with Python 3.11: an e-book library to upload, organize, read in the browser and send to readers, kept in a Calibre library on the drive (Arcana/user/apps/calibre-web/library). Arcana sets the administrator password at the first start and shows it on the Apps page.

license.name: GNU General Public License v3.0 or later
license.notes: Its Python dependencies come from PyPI under their own licenses: BSD, MIT, Apache-2.0, PSF-2.0 and MPL-2.0, except chardet (LGPL-2.1), Unidecode (GPL-2.0-or-later) and iso-639 (AGPL-3.0). The empty Calibre library is Project NOMAD's (Apache-2.0).

resources.title: Stirling PDF
resources.description: Stirling PDF 2.13.1, with Eclipse Temurin Java 25: merge, split, rotate, compress, convert, sign and redact PDF files in the browser, on this computer. This is the openly licensed build (Stirling-PDF.jar), without the login and enterprise features.

license.name: MIT License
